onenight.title: Une nuit
onenight.kicker: One night ashore · pick the town you are nearest · in the order you go
onenight.lede: The Jura dines early: most kitchens take the last orders between half past eight and half past nine, and many close on Sunday and Monday. Lons has its own tables within a few minutes’ walk of each other; Arbois and Pupillin are about forty minutes north by road, Dole further on. Each plan below is one evening in one place. Hours were re-checked on 26 October 2026; where listings disagree, the step says call.
onenight.door_en: Crew ashore for one evening: a plan for each place — the arcades of Lons, the park and rue de Vallière, Arbois on the Cuisance, Pupillin, Dole — in the order you go.
onenight.door_note: L’apéro · la table · le dernier verre

quarters.name: Lons · the arcades and Place de la Liberté
quarters.line: A coffee or a glass facing the theatre, the arcades as the shops close, and a tiny room for the morels.

steps.name: Le Grand Café du Théâtre
steps.text: A glass at the counter of the brasserie facing the theatre, there since 1847. The bar’s evening hours are not confirmed; the kitchen opens at 19:00.

steps.name: Under the arcades
steps.ref: card:Place de la Liberté and the arcades
steps.text: Walk the length of rue du Commerce under the 146 arches, past the plaque at number 24.

steps.name: Ô Tablier
steps.text: The croûte aux morilles au Vin Jaune in a small room below street level. Closed Wednesday and Sunday, dinner only on some nights: listings differ, so call and book.

quarters.after: No table? [[venue:v06-le-bistrot-des-marronniers|Le Bistrot des Marronniers]] is a few streets away on rue de Vallière (closed Sunday).

quarters.name: Lons · the Parc des Bains and rue de Vallière
quarters.line: The salt park in the last light, then meat from the wood grill.

steps.name: The Parc des Bains
steps.ref: card:The Parc des Bains and the Source Salée
steps.text: The old trees round the basin of the salt spring; in late autumn the light goes early, so come before six.

steps.name: Le Bistrot des Marronniers
steps.text: Tablier de sapeur or the pike quenelle, and meat from the wood stove in the room. Closed Sunday; Monday and Saturday hours differ between listings, so ring.

quarters.after: On a concert night, [[card:Le Bœuf sur le Toit|Le Bœuf sur le Toit]] is the town’s music hall: the month’s dates are on the hot board.

quarters.name: Arbois · the Cuisance
quarters.line: A tasting on the square, the river path, then the Bib Gourmand by the water.

steps.name: Domaine Stéphane Tissot
steps.text: The caveau on the Place de la Liberté pours without an appointment: Trousseau, Vin Jaune, Vin de Paille. Its winter hours were not found, so check before you go.

steps.name: Along the Cuisance
steps.text: Down from the square to the river and the bell tower of Saint-Just; a slow half hour.

steps.name: Le Bistronôme
steps.text: The Planches trout ballottine with morels in a Vin Jaune sauce. Dinner Tuesday to Saturday 19:15 to 20:30, and no Thursday dinner from November to March; book.

quarters.after: Cheaper, or on a Sunday: [[venue:v08-la-finette-taverne-d-arbois|La Finette]] on avenue Pasteur, open every day for fondue de Comté and poultry with Vin Jaune.

quarters.name: Pupillin · the village of Ploussard
quarters.line: The pale red at its source, then the starred table opposite the vines.

steps.name: Through the village
steps.text: A short walk through the village that calls itself the world capital of Ploussard; the cooperative cellar keeps daytime hours, so come earlier if you want to taste there.

steps.name: La Table du Grapiot
steps.text: Bresse poultry with Vin Jaune and morels on the longer menus, Ploussard by the glass. One Michelin star since March 2026; closed Monday, and Sunday dinner differs between listings: book by phone.

quarters.after: Cheaper instead: [[venue:v08-la-finette-taverne-d-arbois|La Finette]] in Arbois, a few minutes down the hill.

quarters.name: Dole · the canal and the starred house
quarters.line: The tanners’ canal at dusk, then a starred menu at the end of the week.

steps.name: The canal and the old town
steps.text: The Canal des Tanneurs and the collegiate tower; Pasteur’s birthplace is closed for the winter after 1 November.

steps.name: La Chaumière
steps.text: The gastronomic menu is served only from Friday evening to Saturday evening; on other nights the same house runs as a bistrot. Listings show it closed Sunday and Monday: book.

getaway.title: Le week-end
getaway.door_en: Friday night to Sunday afternoon: the arcades and a small room for the morels, Château-Chalon and Arbois, a starred dinner at Pupillin, the cirque of Baume on Sunday.
getaway.door_note: Le pont la nuit · le marché · la cave · la table
getaway.kicker: The getaway weekend · Friday night to Sunday afternoon
getaway.lede: What the Jura sells is a bottle of Vin Jaune in a souvenir shop and a fondue on a terrace. The real thing takes a car and a little planning: a cellar where the person pouring made the wine, Comté cut at three ages, a starred kitchen in the village of Ploussard, and a walk under the cliffs. The plan stays in Lons on Friday, drives the slope on Saturday with a driver, and ends at the reculée on Sunday. Every stop is in this guide, checked in October 2026.
book: [[venue:v01-la-table-du-grapiot|La Table du Grapiot]] — Saturday dinner, by phone, as soon as you have dates
[[venue:v02-le-bistron-me|Le Bistronôme]] — Saturday lunch; it is a small room
[[venue:v03-tablier|Ô Tablier]] — Friday dinner; call, the listings disagree on its nights
[[card:Domaine Macle|Domaine Macle]] — a Saturday-morning appointment, by phone; bring cash
A driver for Saturday: the plan tastes in three places

stops.name: Under the arcades of rue du Commerce
stops.ref: card:Place de la Liberté and the arcades
stops.text: The long arcaded street of golden stone, the plaque at number 24 where Rouget de Lisle was born, and the clock tower at the end.
stops.meta: Rue du Commerce, Lons · free · on foot

stops.name: Dinner at Ô Tablier
stops.text: The croûte aux morilles au Vin Jaune, then the duck with Macvin, in a small room below the street.
stops.meta: 20 rue Émile Monot · about 36–42 € a head (Oct 2026) · closed Wednesday and Sunday; book

days.label: Saturday
days.title: The rock, the river and the star

stops.name: The Saturday market
stops.text: The smaller Saturday-morning food market on the Cours Sully; the big one is Thursday. Then a Morbier from the family under the arcades, if their door is open.
stops.meta: Cours Sully, Saturday morning · stall prices vary

stops.name: Chocolate at Pelen
stops.text: An écureuil to eat now and a box of Galet de Chalain for later.
stops.meta: 1 rue Saint-Désiré · Saturday 09:00–12:30 by one listing; call

stops.name: Château-Chalon
stops.text: The village on its rock above the vines that make only Vin Jaune; walk to the viewpoints over the slope.
stops.meta: East of Lons by car · free

stops.name: A tasting at Domaine Macle
stops.text: Vin Jaune tasted where it is made, in a family cellar at the top of the village.
stops.meta: 14 rue de la Roche · by appointment only; cash

stops.name: Lunch at Le Bistronôme
stops.text: The trout ballottine with morels in Vin Jaune, by the Cuisance in Arbois.
stops.meta: 62 rue de Faramand, Arbois · lunch 12:15–13:30 · about 35–65 € (Oct 2026)

stops.name: Arbois on foot
stops.text: The river path and the church of Saint-Just; Pasteur’s house on rue de Courcelles may already be closed for the winter, so call first.

stops.name: The Tissot caveau
stops.text: Trousseau, Crémant and Vin de Paille side by side, without an appointment.
stops.meta: 35 Place de la Liberté, Arbois · winter hours not found; check

stops.name: Dinner at La Table du Grapiot
stops.text: The longer menu, for the Bresse poultry with Vin Jaune and morels, and Ploussard from the village.
stops.meta: 3 rue Bagier, Pupillin · menus 60 / 80 / 94 € (Oct 2026) · closed Monday; book

stops.name: The cirque of Baume-les-Messieurs
stops.text: The abbey under the horseshoe of cliffs, then the path along the valley floor to the cascade and the spring.
stops.meta: About 15 km from Lons · 2–3 hours · the show caves are closed until spring

stops.name: Lunch at La Petite Auberge
stops.text: Jura trout with bacon, and the soufflé glacé au Macvin.
stops.meta: 1985 route de Besançon, Lons · Sunday lunch by most listings; call · about 22–47 € (Oct 2026)

stops.name: The salt spring
stops.ref: card:The Parc des Bains and the Source Salée
stops.text: A last walk round the park where the brine that named the town still rises.

more.title: If you have only one evening
more.text: Stay in Lons: the arcades, then [[venue:v03-tablier|Ô Tablier]] or [[venue:v06-le-bistrot-des-marronniers|Le Bistrot des Marronniers]], a few minutes apart.

more.title: The grand night instead
more.text: On a Friday or Saturday, [[venue:v-la-chaumiere|La Chaumière]] in Dole serves its starred menu; the rest of the week it is a bistrot.

more.title: This November
items: Mont d’Or is in season from 10 September to 10 May: buy one at the [[venue:v12-march-de-lons-le-saunier|Thursday market]].
Le Bœuf sur le Toit has concerts on 21, 27 and 28 November: see [[card:Late November at Le Bœuf sur le Toit|the hot board]].
Wednesday 11 November is a public holiday: check every opening.
The Saline royale’s Christmas market opens on 28 November: [[card:Christmas market at the Saline royale|details]].

more.title: Where to sleep
more.text: This guide does not judge hotels, and none of the places in it is one. Lons is the practical base: everything on Friday and Sunday is a short walk or drive from the centre.

more.title: What we would leave out
more.text: A Vin Jaune poured on a café terrace (see [[card:Vin Jaune on a café terrace|the warning]]), pre-cut Comté in plastic, and any list that still sends you to the two-star Jeunet: [[card:The Jeunet name|the house is gone]].
